title: Parallel Octobers
pitch: The visitor chooses a team with a dated early-season record, such as a winless or pointless start, and the page replays its season thousands of times in parallel from the same talent, drawing every path as a branching, root-like fan across the 84-game calendar. Before each reveal the visitor sets a compass needle to forecast the final points; the engine then shows how much of the start was luck on a gauge, and discarding the first games from the sample shows the estimate move.
whyNow: As of 2026-10-12, per several outlets, Calgary is 0-5-0 and the only team without a point, and Philadelphia opened 0-5-2 with a franchise-record seven straight losses; 2026-27 is also the first 84-game season since 1993-94, so old 82-game rules of thumb for how deep a hole is no longer apply.

research.summary: As of 2026-10-12 the NHL season is about two weeks old. Per several outlets, Calgary is 0-5-0 after a 4-2 loss to Anaheim on 2026-10-10 and is the only team without a point, and Philadelphia is 0-5-2 after a 4-1 loss at Carolina on 2026-10-11, a franchise-record seventh straight loss to open a season (the earlier record was set in 1999-00 and matched in 2008-09). The league plays an 84-game schedule this season (1,344 games, 42 home and 42 road per team). PDO (on-ice shooting percentage plus save percentage) is a common luck proxy that drifts toward 100 over large samples. Only the Calgary and Philadelphia records were re-checked; no other real team record is verified, so other clubs in the page are simulated or fictional and each real record carries its as-of date and source.

facts.claim: The 2026-27 NHL regular season is 84 games per team (1,344 games in all, 42 home and 42 road for each club), the first 84-game schedule since 1993-94; it opened Sept. 29, 2026 and runs to April 10, 2027.
PDO is on-ice shooting percentage plus on-ice save percentage; league-wide it balances to 100, so team values far from 100 in short samples are read as luck and tend to drift back toward 100.

As of 2026-10-11, per Canadian Press (CTV News) and the NHL.com Ducks recap, Calgary is 0-5-0 after a 4-2 loss to Anaheim on 2026-10-10, its first season opening with five straight losses, and is the only NHL team without a point.

As of 2026-10-11, per AP, the Philadelphia Inquirer and Broad Street Hockey, Philadelphia lost 4-1 at Carolina for a franchise-record seventh straight loss to open the season (record 0-5-2, so two of the losses came in overtime or a shootout), after a 7-0 opener, outscored 28-8.

inspirations: fan charts in election and weather forecasting

design.coreLoop: Each round presents a team and its dated start. The visitor drags a compass needle (direction = expect a recovery or a slump, length = confidence) to forecast final points, optionally discards early games to test how fragile the read is, then commits. A web worker runs 1,000 seeded season paths from a posterior over team talent; paths are drawn as a branching fan, the forecast is scored with a proper scoring rule, and a luck gauge says how much of the start was PDO noise. Streaks and a calibration chart reward the tenth round because the visitor learns to trust fewer games less.
sophisticationHooks: Grid posterior over team talent: a prior from a hand-set tier rating times a likelihood from the dated early record, so a 0-5-2 start moves the estimate far less than intuition says
Seeded Poisson goal model with overtime and shootout logic and the loser point, run in a worker for 1,000 paths of 84 games, with a simulated field for the playoff line
Proper scoring (log or CRPS-style) with a calibration curve over the visitor's rounds, plus the discard-games slider showing how the estimate shifts
Branching fan chart on canvas where path density forms a mycelium-like network and a compass dial doubles as the input
design.scopeForOneDay: Build the talent posterior (grid), a seeded season-path engine in a worker (1,000 paths, simple Poisson goals plus overtime point), canvas fan chart, compass input, proper scoring and URL-hash share. Real-team content is limited to the two re-checked records (Calgary 0-5-0 and Philadelphia 0-5-2, each shown with its as-of date and source); everything else is fictional teams from a seeded generator, labelled as simulation. Cut: live data, a full 32-team playoff simulation, player-level stats, a calibration curve beyond a simple running score if time is short.
risks: Only the Calgary and Philadelphia records were re-checked (2026-10-12); the page shows them as 'as of 2026-10-11, per <outlet>' and carries no other real record, so unverified standings never appear as fact
Talent priors are hand-set estimates, not data; the page labels them as estimates and keeps fictional teams available so no real-team claim depends on them
Could read as a simulator: the forecasting game and scoring stay central rather than a free-form sandbox
News-bound start records go stale within days; the snapshot is dated and fictional-team mode keeps the page useful, hence durable false
Probability output is labelled 'simulated, not a prediction service, not betting advice'; real team names appear as plain text with no logos

verification.notes: Calgary and Philadelphia records, the 84-game schedule and PDO were each re-found in independent search results; the Calgary game date was corrected to 2026-10-10 and Philadelphia's record is 0-5-2 (not 0-7); the hockey-reference goal-difference snapshot and other hot starts could not be re-found and were removed. Posterior plus worker simulation is ambitious but cut to 1,000 paths and two real teams.
